summary.oneLiner: One of India's oldest and leading manufacturers of starch and starch derivatives, operating as a one-stop B2B solutions provider to food, pharmaceutical and industrial customers from a pan-India manufacturing footprint.
summary.business: Sukhjit Starch and Chemicals Limited, established in 1943 in Phagwara, Punjab, manufactures starch and starch derivatives from maize, having evolved from corn-grinding operations into an integrated starch solutions provider over eight decades. It operates four manufacturing units across India and serves a diverse spectrum of industries as a B2B partner, supplying native starch, modified/derivative starches and allied by-products used in food & beverage, pharmaceutical, paper, textile and other industrial applications.

currentContext.expansion: The Company has grown its manufacturing footprint progressively since 1943, from corn-grinding operations in Phagwara to four manufacturing units across India. A new manufacturing unit was commissioned in Punjab in 2020 with a maize grinding capacity of 600 TPD, undertaken as part of a major expansion programme with capex of approximately Rs.350 crore. Capacity was also expanded over time at the Malda unit (maize grinding capacity increased from 150 TPD to 450 TPD), the Nizamabad unit (150 TPD to 250 TPD) and the Gurplah unit (150 TPD to 300 TPD), alongside earlier enhancement of Phagwara/Nizamabad capacity from 100 TPD to 150 TPD; the Company's combined maize-grinding capacity across its four units now stands at over 1,600 TPD. During FY26 the Company incurred capital expenditure of Rs.12.96 crore on balancing/upgrading its existing manufacturing facilities. For FY2026-27, the Board has approved capital expenditure of Rs.30 crore for modernizing key equipment across units to improve operations and scale up efficiencies at existing locations, to be funded from internal accruals. Management also continues to evaluate greenfield and brownfield expansion opportunities in line with long-term market demand and growth visibility, while maintaining a disciplined and measured investment approach; the Company's R&D collaborations with agricultural universities, seed companies and progressive farmers on high-yield maize varieties are aimed at supporting its expansion into higher-value, margin-accretive applications.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and pricing risk
risks.note: Maize is the Company's primary input; its price is volatile due to climatic factors, government policies and competing demand (including ethanol production), which can pressure input costs and margins.

risks.risk: Climate risk on raw material supply
risks.note: Adverse weather conditions such as erratic monsoons, floods or droughts can impact agricultural output and the availability of maize, the Company's key raw material.

The Indian starch industry has both organised and unorganised players; this competitive intensity leads to pricing pressure, particularly in commoditised product segments, and can affect market share and profitability.
Variability in demand from end-user industries such as FMCG, pharma, paper and textiles may affect sales volumes and realisations.

risks.risk: Global trade and export demand uncertainty
risks.note: The industry is exposed to global trade dynamics including geopolitical tensions, shifting trade policies and tariff changes; risk of low-cost imports and tariff structure changes can affect domestic competitiveness and export demand.

Sustainable operations require ongoing water conservation and responsible water usage; the Company has flagged this as a risk requiring recycling, rainwater harvesting and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) measures.
Elevated inventory levels expose the Company to raw-material price fluctuations and increased carrying costs, requiring calibrated inventory strategy and working capital management.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- H1 margins were impacted by maize price volatility (driven by ethanol-producer demand) and by lower realisations from pricing pressure on finished goods and subdued demand in certain sectors; H2 showed healthy operational traction on firming demand and a stabilising pricing environment
- Maize prices corrected and stabilised in H2, providing a more predictable cost environment compared to H1, though packing material costs saw some impact from the Middle East crisis while finished goods prices remained relatively steady
- Management anticipates a good increase in sales with improved margins in the current year, supported by stable raw material trends, firming product demand and supportive finished-goods pricing
- Early indications of maize price moderation are encouraging, but forecasts of a below-normal monsoon warrant a measured and cautious outlook on the agricultural landscape
- Well-established procurement network, multi-location manufacturing footprint and disciplined inventory management are expected to provide strategic flexibility and supply-chain resilience
- India's strong economic fundamentals, rising demand from key end-use industries and improving export competitiveness (driven by alignment of domestic maize prices with global markets) are expected to provide a supportive growth environment
- Structural drivers such as growth in processed food, pharmaceuticals and exports are expected to support industry expansion, alongside a gradual shift towards higher value-added products
- Rising demand for processed foods, growth in pharmaceutical/nutraceutical sectors and increasing adoption of sustainable packaging are creating opportunities for starch derivatives and specialty ingredients
- Growing preference for clean-label, plant-based and functional ingredients is expanding the addressable market for higher-value, application-driven products

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has grown its manufacturing footprint progressively since 1943, from corn-grinding operations in Phagwara to four manufacturing units across India. A new manufacturing unit was commissioned in Punjab in 2020 with a maize grinding capacity of 600 TPD, undertaken as part of a major expansion programme with capex of approximately Rs.350 crore. Capacity was also expanded over time at the Malda unit (maize grinding capacity increased from 150 TPD to 450 TPD), the Nizamabad unit (150 TPD to 250 TPD) and the Gurplah unit (150 TPD to 300 TPD), alongside earlier enhancement of Phagwara/Nizamabad capacity from 100 TPD to 150 TPD; the Company's combined maize-grinding capacity across its four units now stands at over 1,600 TPD. During FY26 the Company incurred capital expenditure of Rs.12.96 crore on balancing/upgrading its existing manufacturing facilities. For FY2026-27, the Board has approved capital expenditure of Rs.30 crore for modernizing key equipment across units to improve operations and scale up efficiencies at existing locations, to be funded from internal accruals. Management also continues to evaluate greenfield and brownfield expansion opportunities in line with long-term market demand and growth visibility, while maintaining a disciplined and measured investment approach; the Company's R&D collaborations with agricultural universities, seed companies and progressive farmers on high-yield maize varieties are aimed at supporting its expansion into higher-value, margin-accretive applications.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of India's oldest and leading starch manufacturers with over eight decades of industry experience and long-standing customer relationships
- Pan-India, multi-location manufacturing footprint (four units) enabling proximity to raw material sources and demand centres, minimising supply chain disruption
- Integrated manufacturing capabilities and a diversified product portfolio spanning native starch, dextrines, pre-gel starch, liquid glucose, malto-dextrin, dextrose and sorbitol
- Centralised, dedicated R&D centre at Phagwara driving customer-focused innovation and application-specific solutions across food, pharmaceutical and industrial segments
- Experienced, promoter-led management team providing strong strategic direction and operational expertise
- Early-adopter environmental initiatives (biogas/biomass-based energy, hydrogen generation from biogas process effluents) supporting cleaner, more sustainable operations
